page: Microsoft Azure DC32eds_v6 is an x86_64 virtualization instance provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V with dedicated Intel CPU resources. The configuration supplies 32 vCPUs paired with 128 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. Unlike diskless instance tiers, the DC32eds_v6 integrates 1890 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage directly on the host hardware. It features no dedicated GPU hardware accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network routing for external ingress.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency perspective, the bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD volume eliminates the expense of attaching separate non-persistent block devices for high-throughput scratch space. However, local storage on Hyper-V instances operates as ephemeral capacity, meaning critical application data requires replication or persistent remote storage integration. With a balanced resource footprint, the server allocates solid per-core RAM density without the price overhead typically demanded by extreme memory-heavy instance classes.

This balance of multi-core Intel processing, 128 GB of RAM, and fast local NVMe storage positions the DC32eds_v6 effectively for I/O-intensive workloads requiring rapid local cache or scratch disks. Key target environments include relational and transactional database servers, large-scale build and CI/CD runners, distributed caching layers, ETL data processing jobs, and moderate enterprise web serving systems that benefit from fast local storage.
description: Microsoft Azure DC32eds_v6 is a general-purpose virtualization instance hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V, delivering 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel processor. The system is equipped with 128 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, and integrates 1890 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without hardware GPU acceleration and does not include complimentary public IPv4 networking. The inclusion of substantial local NVMe storage provides low-latency disk throughput for temporary file structures, high-frequency logging, or ephemeral database processing without incurring secondary block-attachment costs. These hardware characteristics make the DC32eds_v6 suitable for database operations, ETL data pipelines, software compilation pipelines, and transactional enterprise applications that demand substantial multi-threaded compute alongside fast local disk I/O.
